decision: The catastrophe is both intent and accident: the Essart was deliberate, the Breaking an accident triggered by one holder's refusal.
why: Keeps magic a tool and blame honestly mixed, so no villain explains the world.

decision: Magic is five ordered rules (move not make, ash tithe, like calls like, anchors, sense as heaviest coin) relearned in order, with the thing under the land as the one place the Tally fails.
why: Gives the optimizer exploitable rules and Sanderson's first law, while keeping the eldritch edge unexplained.

decision: The player is the holder of the Hollow keel, a battery chosen for never refusing, who forgets at each Black Drift and wakes in the ruins of previous towns.
why: The amnesiac turn that lowers status rather than making a villain or hero, and explains 'again' without a loop.

decision: Turns are spent on exactly four tropes; every other trope resolves as promised.
why: decisions.md tropes rule: subverting everything is confusing and dull.

decision: The burn keeps survivors alive along seams, so the obvious fix would kill everyone.
why: Follows the premise's consequences honestly (a sunless world must be warmed somehow) and kills the obvious goal mid-game.

decision: Seasons are the burn breathing: a 21-day cycle of Still, Drift and Clear, with Black Drifts as lore only.
why: A season fact of the broken world that changes play; no countdown.

decision: Five regions as five acts, each answering one question, with one linked-group cascade target per region.
why: The reveals fall into five questions and ~2.5 weeks each matches the pacing strawman.

decision: The bestiary rests on three rules: the Taking, seam life, made things.
why: Makes the creatures one fauna following from biology, per decisions.md.

decision: The dead god is implied by six details and never named or revealed.
why: Godsgrave guardrail: leave it implied and strange, never spelled out.

decision: The running motif is a wobbly stool that is never fixed and never explained.
why: A signature joke that later becomes evidence of 'again'.

decision: The ending is a Hearth held by many, with three core variants chosen once at O-final and six strands varying the epilogue.
why: One informed choice whose menu is decided by what was built; no karma meter.

decision: Notables are fixed (same every save) or risen (authored role, cast per save).
why: The spine needs fixed people; risen ones let each save's town own its notables.

decision: 53 spine beats over 84 days, a weekly beat every week and four beats a week from week 4, with the back half revealing the player.
why: decisions.md: the back half never slows; reveals get bigger, not sparser.

decision: Player death is a mechanic from B20: return to the warm stone, no cost, progression once.
why: Grim Dawn ceiling, within decisions.md's death guardrails.

decision: Author: one informed choice near the end is fine.
why: Open question 2, answered.

decision: Author: go with the three-week season cycle and let the simulator and play test it.
why: Open question 3, answered.

decision: Author: uncanny wrongness in ordinary animals (behaviour, not gore) is fair game.
why: Open question 5, answered.

decision: Author: the writing team names everything, the world and the starting valley included.
why: Open question 6, answered.

decision: Author: a quiet, sad ending for the player's character, chosen knowingly, is allowed.
why: Open question 1, answered.

decision: Author: the writing team decides the player-death mechanic and the home/expedition balance late on, unseen by him.
why: Open questions 4 and 7, answered without looking.

decision: Canon is held as keyed facts in canon.jsonl; only the lead writes canon, and proposals are checked against the ids they touch.
why: Rereading prose is a weak continuity check; studios keep keyed continuity records.

decision: OPEN: N3 'declines every offer' conflicts with O-book being accepted and with E-c calling N3's yes their first.
why: Either O-book means the player leaves the book (no acceptance by N3), or the refusal tell needs an exception; E-c's 'first yes' must hold. Task T3.

decision: OPEN: N3's keel failed and snapped back, yet N3 is unageing and forgets daily; rule 4 says a let-go anchor releases the moved thing, and only a holder of a standing keel is said not to age.
why: Magic solves nothing outside its rules; the mechanism must follow from rules 4 and 5. Task T3.

decision: OPEN: B1 says the journal is blank past the torn pages, but world.md has old margin notes in the player's hand already in it (first surfacing at B9).
why: Needs a rule for how old-hand notes exist in a blank book (e.g. they surface on entries as they open). Task T4.

decision: OPEN: timeline gaps. The last Black Drift was months before day 1, yet the player wakes on day 1 alone in fresh ruins; where the last town's people went and what the months held is unsaid. Also 'every few years' vs 'once every several years', whether holders forgot during the thirty good years, and whether 'at least the fourth time' fits forty years.
why: A dated chronology is needed before clues and N9's and B16's histories can be fair. Task T9.

decision: OPEN: N9 is said to arrive at belonging tier, but by B34 (day 50) the town is at self-actualization (P8, day 48).
why: Either she is a belonging-kind arrival drawn by the hall at any tier, or the tier note is wrong. Task T9.

decision: OPEN: F1's cause is a rare out-of-place creature drawn by chance; if none comes before the palisade is maxed, F1 has no cause.
why: A side beat needs a cause that exists on every save. Task T10.

decision: OPEN: season set pieces are promised as side beats but none are written, and decisions.md requires each season to carry its own stories and quests sized to last.
why: Thin where the drip between spine beats depends on it. Task T10.

decision: Beats carry flat-story fields (turn, outcome, opens/advances/pays, cost, moves, thread, register); the beat key for system unlocks is renamed unlocks so opens means promises; outcome values are quoted because YAML 1.1 reads bare yes/no as booleans.
why: docs/research/flat-story.md; no code reads beats.yaml yet, so the rename breaks nothing.

decision: Promises and questions get ids C-promise-1..15 in canon; an open promise must be advanced or paid within 14 days; Q4 counts as paid by the scream (felt, never answered).
why: Promises without visible progress read as going nowhere; 14 days is two weeks of play.

decision: 14 single-counter gates (B5, B6, B7, B9, B12, B15, B16, B19, B20, B23, B28, B38, B46, B47) now pair the counter with a story precondition or a second quality; target days unchanged.
why: Single-quality gates make grind; the pairing also encodes story order the beats already assumed.

decision: ACCEPTED EXCEPTION: B2 keeps a single-counter gate (scavenging 3).
why: Day one teaches with one action; nothing else exists to pair it with, and it lands within minutes. Superseded by D-45: B2 is now gated on the fire action.

decision: Turn directions set so weeks 1-10 never net up and no three run one way: clock beats B8 and B13 turn up; B6, B7, B14, B17 end down on a cost; B21, B31, B39 end up.
why: The measured upward drift of LLM stories is this story's biggest risk; three-in-a-row was present in the draft's reading (B30-B32, B40-B42, B46-B47 with B44).

decision: Every week now holds a no or no-and: B4, B12, B15, B19, B20, B22, B27, B28, B32, B34, B38, B44, B46, B50; no two clean yeses in a row.
why: Clean wins stop a story; try-fail keeps it moving. The draft had whole weeks of clean success.

decision: Costs added so every week pays in at least two kinds: B17 and B45 lose a light-tier life, B18 spoils food, B26 spends the waystation ward, B35 sets a steep price, B38 hollows an expedition member.
why: A week with no cost, or one kind of cost, is flat; all losses stay on the light tier per the Never list.

decision: The mirror moves into B40; B41 becomes the keepers' standing orders, which a holder can use to stand them down.
why: B40-B42 were three downs in a row; the keepers' orders were already promised readable in R4 (creatures.md) and had no beat.

decision: The Q5 trail gets visible steps: the circles sign on the stranger's table (B16), a Chequer plan in the keel chamber (B30), the sign in the layers (B36), a pencil tick in the registry (B40), old cairns on the lamp road (B45).
why: Q5 went 40 days untouched between B12 and B36 in the draft.

decision: N3's trail gets steps: the flinch at hold moves to B21, N6's glance at N3's wrist (B29), N3 asks for letters (B33), N3 won't cross the causeway (B37).
why: The stranger promise went over two weeks unadvanced between B24 and B42.

decision: Fixed notables are placed in beats so none goes two weeks unmoved (N1 at B29, B32, B36, B37, B44, B45; N4 at B27, B36, B38, B44, B47; N9 at B40, B44, B49; N8 at B42, B49); risen notables N2, N5, N7 stay at two spine beats or fewer and their arcs live in side beats (T5).
why: A recurring character unmoved for two weeks reads as forgotten; risen notables' arcs are save-cast and belong in side beats, which the route check will include.

decision: Fourteen threads (th-survive, th-yes, th-burn, th-magic, th-past, th-network, th-stranger, th-self, th-faith, th-seams, th-mentor, th-chequer, th-dark, th-hearth), each with a start and an end.
why: Orphan beats and threads that never end are flat-story flags.

decision: content/team/flatcheck.py checks the authored order and takes --route for simulated routes; it reads accepted exceptions from this log.
why: A later code agent runs it per sharp, typical and lazy route.

decision: T1 front page final: 8 lines, 5 from revision A and 3 from revision B, ordered as one scene (place, sky, no name, flint, a failed spark, a fire, lingering inside, the fire low behind you). Four lines reworded to clear 3-word echoes of bible prose; B's name line swapped for A's because patting yourself down would find the book.
why: B's closing pair carries the turn as an unstated cost; A's middle supplies the try-fail on the fire. All ids within T1's first-hour allowance; no banned words; n-gram check zero against content/ prose.

decision: Day 1 opens on one-off narrative actions (A1-A7, projects of kind action) instead of a lone Scavenge button: stand up, look around, search the coat, gather wood by hand, dry it, strike a fire, knap an edge.
why: Author direction and decisions.md 'The first minutes are slow, made by hand, and told': the player feels the character's weakness first; systems.md models these as projects.

decision: Tools before skills: Woodcutting opens only after a flint edge is knapped (A7); before that, wood is gathered by hand.
why: Author direction: no woodcutting without a tool.

decision: The first fire's failure is deterministic: damp wood never lights, dry wood always does; the drying action is offered before flint is found, so a player who dries first never fails, and the log's wry line lands only on striking early.
why: Author flag 1 and 'Chance shows, preparation decides'; the joke then sits on the player's own choice.

decision: B2's gate is the fire action (A6), not a bare skill counter; the B2 single-counter exception is retired.
why: The fire action is a real precondition and the flint inside it still needs scavenging 3.

decision: The first craft is a choice between a stool and a windbreak, both affordable; a wry line about putting a seat before shelter fires only when the player picks the stool with the windbreak affordable.
why: Author flag 2: humor only on choices the player made.

decision: The mix arrives when drying runs alongside scavenging, and standing orders arrive on the fire's falling fuel line; each is introduced in the UI by the thing that needs it.
why: Author direction 5 and 'Taught by need, and needed again'.

decision: Standing up (A1) is three short pushes, a log line each, the third succeeding, instead of one long silent bar.
why: Author note 1: the player must see the needle move.

decision: The cold is established on looking around (A2) with a cold status that clears when the fire lights, so gathering wood has a visible purpose and stays the player's choice.
why: Author note 2.

decision: The coat holds a charcoal stub with the book; writing is never a mechanic.
why: Author note 3; charcoal fits a world of fire and ash.

decision: Drying no longer blocks: it runs while the player finds flint, clears a spot (A6) and rings it with stones (A7), so the wood is dry about when the ring is done; bars are seconds.
why: Author note 4 and decisions.md 'The opening is 15-30 minutes of near-constant interaction'.

decision: Strike (A8) is offered once the ring is done, before the wood is dry; the wet-wood joke lands only on a player who strikes early.
why: Author note 5: humor on the player's own choice; the failure stays deterministic.

decision: Stool and windbreak each carry a visible tradeoff and cost when chosen (stool: faster rest, fire open to the wind; windbreak: longer-burning fire, slow rest; each 3 dry wood from the fire's fuel); the other is built later.
why: Author note 6 and decisions.md 'No option is perfect; every choice is a tradeoff'.

decision: Roasting roots in the coals (A10) opens Cooking on day 1, so hunger is answered inside the opening.
why: The opening needs steps up to the leave-it-running moment, and food was the remaining need.

decision: The stool's counterpart is a fireback (stacked stone behind the fire, holding its heat) rather than a windbreak.
why: Day 1 falls in the Still, which has no wind (C-season-2); the tradeoff stays: the fireback makes the fire burn longer, the stool makes rest faster.

decision: B3 lands at day one's end, on its last visit: gated on P0's last stage (P0.4, Take stock), which requires the larder, the smoking rack, H7, smoked >= 6 and roots >= 15 in the card's own requires; typical routes 20-28 game hours after the opening's end, babysitter 6-8, lazy 30-40.
why: The first arrival is the payoff the whole day builds toward (smoke, a visit, a trade, food to spare); one card's requires holds the conjunction, so no new condition kind is needed.

decision: The R1 old-snares clue is softened on day one (H4): an old snare in the same run, decades old and rusted through, with nothing about whose it was or how it was tied; the 'set your way' version waits until after B9, and N9 pays the thread at B34.
why: Q2 opens at B9 (C-promise-2); a snare tied the player's way on day 2 would open it a week early. Opening C-promise-2 at H4 instead was considered and rejected for the same reason.

decision: H7's trade (three roots gone, a strip of smoked meat left) is a story cost, never a penalty for absence: it fires on its own timer after H6 whether the player is watching or away, takes and leaves the same, needs roots >= 3 so it is always whole, and its lines are true either way. decisions.md's 'nothing is lost while you're away' is read as nothing lost because you were away.
why: Spine beats already take stores as story costs (B3, B7, B18, B22) on routes where nobody watches; what the rule forbids is absence causing the loss.

decision: Change from opening-v2: the near question (C-promise-16, who is out there) is advanced on every day-one visit and answered at the last, by B3, instead of being answered in the next session. V3's advance is H5's lean-to facing the ridge; flatcheck checks every visit.
why: Day one runs on the story's clock across several sessions; a question answered in the second session would leave four visits with no pull. A promise touched every visit keeps it alive without spending a deep-pull beat.

decision: Cooking's skill row opens with the smoking rack (P0.3) on day one, not at A10; the roast stays the first cooking act. Amends D-55's 'opens Cooking'.
why: The shipped opening's roast opens no skill and is locked; a skill row with one one-off would train nothing. Canon now matches what shipped.

decision: At B3 N1 sits at the fire on the player's side; the far side of the fire stays B6's.
why: B6 has her sit on the far side that night (C-beat-6), which reads only as a move away from where she usually sits.

decision: V2 and V3 get real work instead of waits. V2: a new one-off A14 (the camp by daylight, after the first snare) brings the lean-to and the larder into view, so H5, the build-order choice, the mix switch and When ready move from V3 into V2. The larder becomes mostly stone (4 dry wood, 12 stones) and the lean-to mostly wood (10 dry wood, 2 stones), so the builds' need is a mix switch, not one card laid four times. V3: the rack opens on the first catch (the absence's one unlock); smoke_roots opens with the rack instead of at H7; a roots order card 'under 15 -> Forage, until 15' is offered once Take stock shows and the larder is built. The B3 visit stays short until day two is built (held, accepted).
why: The simulator's per_visit check: V2 ended within a minute of the return and idled waiting for the first catch; V3 waited on the first smoke and laid wood four times running. Each fix is a step on a need the player can see (the camp by day, Take stock's roots and smoked needs), reusing existing kinds: a one-off card, crafts, an order card, a lane card. Fits into: cards, order cards; no new system.

decision: Day one's chain runs on the player's setup: the rack opens at A14 beside the two builds (t_rack stays for a player who left before A14) and is built of green poles (10 damp wood, not dry), so it goes up in V2 without a run of wood laying, smoke_roots opens with the first smoke_catch completion (H6's condition) instead of with the rack, and Take stock opens on H7's own condition (t_stock_open renamed t_stock_shown) so the two are one moment. Amends D-63's 'the rack opens on the first catch' and 'smoke_roots opens with the rack'.
why: Every day-one unlock landed at a fixed time whatever the setup (docs/decisions.md, 'Unlocks mostly come from play'). Built in V2, the rack lets the catch rule smoke while the player is away, so H6, H7 and B3 come hours sooner with the rule than without, while H1 and H2 keep the story's clock. smoke_roots waits for the first smoke so the first smoke is always meat, which H6 and the visitor need.

decision: The ending is E-d: the Hollow keel is remade as the Hearth, still anchored by the player, its upkeep paid from the town's remembrance of its dead, entered by name in N8's roll; the town keeps the names and loses the faces. E-a (many hands) is cut; E-b and E-c stay.
why: The old ending was the stock sacrifice cycle broken by sharing the cost. Sharing among the living now fails by cascade (B49), and the answer is a line the Chequer's own costing struck out (team/rework-plan.md, §1).

decision: B40's selection field reads, in effect, present, no dependants, and the tick beside 'offered self' is in the player's own hand: the player volunteered. The mirror is cut (amends D-36).
why: 'Will not refuse' read as BioShock's conditioning and took the yes away; this hands it back, so the joke stays about choices the player made.

decision: Turns are spent on five tropes: the four in D-4 plus the ending (sharing already failed; the town's remembrance pays). The town pays for how it ends, rather than pulling together. Amends D-4.
why: The pre-read filed the ending as the worn sacrifice cycle; the new ending is the turn.

decision: Chronology before day 1: the Essart ~70 years; thirty good years; the Breaking ~40; town 1 (40-~30), town 2 (~30-20), town 3 (~20-10, the failed shared keel), town 4 (~10 years to months); Black Drifts every 9 to 12 years, none forgetting in the good years; this is the fourth time. Resolves D-25.
why: Clues, N9's history and B16's stranger need dated towns to be fair; the ruin woken in is town 4's, whose small town left.

decision: N3 declines only what would keep or bind them (a place in a house, a hand, a rope to hold, a name) and accepts what asks nothing back, the book included; sleeves down, no flinch. E-c's yes is their first binding yes. Resolves D-22.
why: 'Declines every offer' contradicted O-book's acceptance and E-c's first yes.

decision: N3's mechanism: when they let go, the keel's load cascaded away, but the part of the working that holds its holder had nothing left to hold, so it keeps itself on N3's own memory, one day at a time. Resolves D-23.
why: Follows from rules 4 and 5 without a new rule: the hold on the holder is its own small held working.

decision: The journal's later pages were never blank: a few carry small pencil notes near the gutter, found as entries reach them. Old-ink notes come from the selves of towns 2 to 4, may contradict each other and are not always right; old_hand_rate's description changes, not its rate. Resolves D-24.
why: Squares with the shipped line, which says only that the first page after the torn ones isn't quite blank, and drops the always-right previous self (a Torment convention).

decision: The circles-round-a-circle diagram shows three times only: P6, B24 and B49. It is cut at B12, B16, B30 and B36; the Q5 trail runs instead on the B12 and B30 tallies, B16's re-tied snares and B36's stools. Amends D-37.
why: Seven showings made the glyph a stock breadcrumb; three keep it a puzzle.

decision: N3's trail steps: binding offers declined (B19), no hand in N4's prayer ring (B21), won't stay the night at the waystation (B24), doesn't take N6's hand (B29), copies the keel name off their wrist (B33), won't cross the causeway (B37). The flinch at 'hold' and N6's glance at N3's wrist are cut. Amends D-38.
why: The flinch was a tell that named the answer; declines of binding things keep the trail and hide the mark until B33.

decision: Q4's cues: the cooling, the breathing, the faith's taboo never thank the warmth, and B47's even draw with its journal figures. The ribs, the ridges' spacing, the dunes' shape, 'don't wake it' and the scream are cut; Q4 counts as paid by the even draw. The word 'god' appears nowhere in canon or text. Amends D-9 and D-30.
why: The ribs and the scream were the dead-god image the pre-read filed as worn (a corpse-shaped landscape); the even draw is felt and never explained.

decision: B32's cost becomes people (was option): the player holds a seam shut and the logging post on the same seam freezes, killing a light-tier worker. B49's turn becomes down (was up). Within D-33 and D-35: flatcheck adds no flag on target days or on routes scaled 0.83x and 1.17x.
why: B32's lesson now comes through a cost the player caused; B49 records a failure.

decision: B35 adds the Warm's custom: the elder scratches a porter's wife's name on the crack's lip and says it into the crack; side beat SB-face (4 days after B35) shows the lost face and opens O-price (ask the Warm to stop, or let it stand), which moves no progress; strand S-seam reads O-price.
why: The cost of E-d shows as a custom happening to someone before anyone chooses it, not as a menu.

decision: The founding event is the Essart (was the Kindling; briefly the Assart).
why: 'Kindling' is Dark Souls' bonfire word in an ash world with a warm stone you return to. 'Assart' reads by its parts as a joke; essart is the Anglo-French form of the same word, with the same Exchequer link (team/names.jsonl).

decision: The Chequer seal on a holder's wrist shuts that mind's links to a working's draw, so a draw on a holder stops at the holder; holders were picked present, no dependants for that reason. Town 3's sharers had no seals.
why: Without it, every Black Drift's draw on the anchor should have cascaded into the town (team/ending-check-2.jsonl).

decision: The Warm read their dead's names off the lip of a seam crack, where generations of names are scratched into the rock, and at B35 the elder scratches the wife's name before saying it. A draw on a memory of the dead stops only at the burned dead.
why: A name survives a draw only if written; spoken lists that kept their names would contradict the rule. The Taking says an unburned body still carries sense (team/ending-check-2.jsonl).

decision: Leave is given per name, not per household or town: each household brings the names it gives, and a household that refuses keeps its dead's faces. The Hall resists, which shows in who isn't in B51's queue and in S-names. N6's note (every household's leave) stays as his wrong premise. B51's queue brings names only, no keepsakes or objects.
why: A unanimous queue would make the leave irony tidy; per-name leave fits the Hall's resistance. Objects brought to the table would be Eternal Sunshine's waiting room (team/ending-check-2.jsonl).

decision: C-promise-17 (what can pay instead) opens at B27 and is advanced at B35, B39 and B44 and paid at B50; B11 and B21 plant it without a field.
why: flatcheck flags an advance before the promise opens (promise_unopened at B21), and B27 is where the question is first raised.

decision: Day two runs from B3 to B4 (story day 2's evening, the second night, story day 3) and ends on B4 with a feature card that says out of fiction that this is as far as the game goes for now; day one's end card loses its 'still being written' line once day two ships.
why: Canon has only B4 between B3 and B5, and B4's no_and closes the near question H3 opened; ending on it, as day one ends on B3, gives day three a fresh pull (the wolves know where the camp is).

decision: From B3 N1 works on a lane of her own (n1), with her own versions of the gathering cards (base rate, no XP, camp items at the hands' rate), run by a rule; B3's outcome sets her default rule (always forage) so she is never idle; changing her task is editing or adding a rule. The town's mix with people as shares waits for a second person.
why: Fit pass: work that runs beside the player's hands is a lane, and a side lane's rule is a single task (decisions.md, The mix), so one person needs no new engine part; a default rule keeps a B3 landed while away from costing anything (the 2 AM test). Fits into: Lanes, Cards, Standing orders.

decision: The evening's clock starts at A15 (giving her the stool, a one-off that glows with B3), not at B3: dusk at A15 + 0.25 game h, night 2 about one game hour, morning 3 at A15 + 1.25 h.
why: B3 often lands while the player is away (queued Take stock); a clock from B3 would bring B3, her lane, the night and the morning in one return, past the two-unlocks-per-absence rule. A15 is always tapped on a visit, so the night always follows a present moment.

decision: Her first rule is offered under the roots line when roots reach 24 while she forages: 24 or more roots, she cuts wood, until under 20 (at_least with release, on lane n1). A second, under the damp wood line once her shelter is in view: under 12, she cuts wood, until 12.
why: A full store wastes her work while the makers keep running (engine DESIGN.txt, Cap), which is the visible need a rule answers, the catch rule's shape. Fits into: order cards.

decision: The town's first choice is A16's two builds (her shelter: she works a fifth faster; a woodstack: twice the dry wood), brought into view by a one-off on morning 3, not a choice paid by Camp 7. Camp 7 pays the wall taking 9; Camp 8 is held and lifted by B4. Amends day-one.md's note that the marker after Camp 6 reads as a choice.
why: Builds that open while the player is away cannot be queued, which breaks the 2 AM test; a one-off on the morning keeps them in view unready, as A14 did. Fits into: cards (crafts), the Camp's levels.

decision: The cart offer (O-cart) opens when her shelter is built and never expires. Its answers are Go (the walk runs on the player's hands, then the first you-said-yes line) and She goes (the same walk on her lane, above her task). Either answer takes the same time, brings nothing back, and lands B4 with the same facts; the you-said-yes line follows only Go.
why: Canon is silent on a no. Declining must cost no progress and the joke lands only after a yes (C-motif-4), so the no sends her instead and the beat stays whole. A find from the walk would make Go the better answer. Fits into: Offers and quests (its first piece), Cards, Gates.

decision: The cart is taken in the second night: J2 is a dragging sound carried from the ridge (no animal named), and the ridge's square leaves the art from J2 on with no line saying so; B4 finds the prints.
why: B4 says the cart was dragged off and the prints are wolves'; the Still carries sound (C-season-2) as H1's howl did, and the art rewards whoever watches the ridge.

decision: Night 2 gets no out-of-fiction wait card; make_room's countdown to first light says when morning comes, as look_out's did. Provisional until asked spoiler-free (day-two.md, Open 5).
why: The player met the real-time night once already with its card; a countdown on the next card states the wait's length (research/waits-and-ends.md) without repeating the explanation.

decision: Day two's near question is C-promise-18 (what is up on the ridge), opened by J1, advanced by J2 and the offer, paid by B4. N1 gives her name at J1, in return for the stool; until then player text says she. The stool touch (C-promise-8) is day two's one deep-pull beat.
why: H3 showed the square and day one never named it, so it is the open gap the player already holds; canon fixes N1's name but not when it is given, and a kindness the player chose is the moment that suits the yes thread B4 opens.

decision: D-85's two order cards become one: under the damp wood line from B3, she cuts wood (at_most 5, release 11, on lane n1). The roots-full card is dropped; a full roots line she feeds is answered by changing her task.
why: An at_least order card taps a card that spends its store (the loader's check, kept), and none of her cards takes roots; a second damp wood card on the same test would be answered by the first. The release stays under the 12 the loader can count on at B3.

decision: The hands' walk (Go) is 14400 s of work, up from 7200, so it takes the same 4 h as her walk (17280 s at her shelter's 1.2) when started rested. D-87's same time is reckoned at a rested start.

decision: Supersedes D-95's placement: the raised bed opens at A15's finish (V1) and is built then; the policies queue no stage while A16 or a build waits, so B4 does not move. Day three, whose V7 had leaned on the bed's last stage, gets its own: the hearth's course takes 10 stones (was 12), under where the track's hold leaves the store, so the first course is queued the return the clay comes in; and a news line 2 h into the bay (t_bay_clock, t_bay_clock_his, t_bay_mid) for a return during its five hours. With the bed out of day three's queue the hearth's first course came a visit earlier and the week ran ahead (B5 3.29, B7 4.98 on typical), so cure_hearth's bar goes 30 000 to 38 000 s, which puts B5, B6 and B7 back where they stood (3.47, 4.29, 5.37); and the track takes 15 roots a run (was 14), since day three's end then left roots losing 52% away 8 h.
why: D-95 assumed V1 was day two's fullest visit. Measured once taps pay exactly, V1 held one tap (the stool) on most routes, with every store full at B3 and nothing to spend them on; the bed is V1's decision. Moving it shifted a bed stage out of day three's V7 and left a return during the bay with nothing new. Proven by toggling: the bed's rest reward off, the hearth's stones back at 12, the bed's bar tripled and the simulator's kept lines off each left B5-B7 where they were; the cure bar moved them.
